plan.contextChunk: This figure is an annotated graph of one full cycle of a transformed sine wave, marked up to expose its midline, amplitude, and period. The vertical y-axis carries ticks from -2 up to 4, the horizontal x-axis is labeled at pi/2 and at pi, and both axes end in arrowheads. The solid dark blue curve leaves the y-axis at height 1, rises to a maximum of 4 a quarter of the way along, falls back through that starting height, bottoms out at -2 near three-quarters of the way, and returns to height 1 at pi. A horizontal orange arrow at the level y = 1 extends rightward from the vertical axis, labeled Midline: y = 1. A vertical teal arrow runs up the curve's peak from that orange level to the maximum, tagged by a leader with Amplitude: |A| = 3. Below the plot, a red double-headed arrow spans the width of the drawn cycle beneath the label Period = pi. The three annotations measure independent things: the vertical center of the oscillation, the stretch away from that center, and the horizontal distance before the shape repeats. Taken together they are the quantities needed to reconstruct the equation of a sinusoid from its picture alone.

interactionPlan.concept: A sinusoid is fully described by three independent quantities — midline (vertical center), amplitude (distance from midline to peak), and period (horizontal repeat length) — each of which can be read off the graph and changed without affecting the others.
elements: y-axis with tick labels from -2 to 4 and arrowhead, labeled y
x-axis with tick labels pi/2 and pi and arrowhead, labeled x
dark blue solid sine curve: one full cycle starting at (0,1), max 4, min -2, returning to (pi,1)
horizontal orange arrow at y = 1 extending rightward from the y-axis, labeled 'Midline: y = 1'
vertical teal arrow from the midline up to the peak of the curve
leader line from the teal arrow to label 'Amplitude: |A| = 3'
red double-headed arrow below the plot spanning one cycle, labeled 'Period = pi'

interactions.label: Amplitude |A|
interactions.teaches: Amplitude is the vertical distance from the midline to the peak (or trough) — the wave stretches and squeezes vertically while the midline stays put

interactions.label: Midline y =
interactions.teaches: The midline is a vertical shift: the entire wave moves up or down with it while its height and width stay unchanged

interactions.label: Period
interactions.teaches: Period is the horizontal length of one complete cycle — the wave stretches or compresses sideways while its vertical shape is untouched

demo_steps.title: Three measurements, one wave
demo_steps.narration: The curve shown is fully described by three numbers visible in the annotations: a midline at y = 1, an amplitude of 3, and a period of pi. Each measures something independent of the others.

demo_steps.title: Amplitude: distance from midline
demo_steps.narration: Drag the amplitude slider: the teal arrow grows or shrinks as the peak and trough move away from or toward the midline — but the orange midline and the cycle's width never move.

demo_steps.title: Midline: vertical center
demo_steps.narration: Drag the midline slider: the orange arrow and the entire wave shift up or down together, while the peak-to-midline distance stays fixed — vertical shift is separate from amplitude.

demo_steps.title: Period: repeat length
demo_steps.narration: Drag the period slider: the red arrow spans more or less of the x-axis as the wave stretches or compresses horizontally, while its height above and below the midline is unchanged.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Midline, amplitude, and period are independent knobs — you can change any one without affecting the other two, and together they uniquely determine the sinusoid's equation.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Standard xy-plane with arrowhead axes; y ticks at -2 through 4, x ticks labeled pi/2 and pi. The blue curve starts at (0, midline), peaks one-quarter period in, crosses the midline at half period, troughs at three-quarters, and ends at (period, midline) — redraw it live from the three slider values. Keep the three annotations color-coded and persistent: orange horizontal midline arrow with its 'Midline: y = k' label updating, teal vertical midline-to-peak arrow with 'Amplitude: |A| = A' label updating, and red double-headed period arrow below the plot with 'Period = ...' updating (pi-style labels are nice but decimal values are acceptable when off defaults). Amplitude slider range keeps peak/trough near the figure's y-extents; period slider spans roughly pi/2 to 2pi.

plan.authoredInteractions:

Inspecting the graph, we can determine that the period is π, the midline is y=1, and the amplitude is 3. See the figure.

A graph of y=3sin(2x)+1. The graph has an amplitude of 3. There is a midline at y=1. There is a period of pi. Local maximum at (pi/4, 4) and local minimum at (3pi/4, -2).

discrepancies: the y-axis integer ticks span roughly 5 down to −3 in the generated figure, while the source frames the wave with ticks only from 4 down to −2 — extra headroom slightly changes the composition
the source's orange midline arrow extends past π close to where the curve ends (~1.25 periods); the generated arrow stops at ~1.06T, so it looks shorter relative to the curve
an equation readout ('y = 1 + 3·sin(2x)') appears in the UI panel, which has no counterpart in the source figure (helpful addition, but extra content)
evaluation.notes: An exemplary reproduction: the curve, axes with arrowheads, x-ticks at π/2 and π, and the three color-coded annotation arrows (teal amplitude, orange midline, red period) all match the source, and the three sliders plus demo-step player correctly demonstrate that midline, amplitude, and period are independent measurements; only trivial framing differences and a helpful extra equation readout separate it from the original.
action_items: Tighten the y-scale padding so integer tick labels run from −2 to 4 instead of roughly −3 to 5, matching the source figure's framing.
Extend the midline arrow endpoint closer to the curve's right edge (e.g., T*1.2) so its length matches the source arrow that reaches past π toward the curve end.
Visually demote the UI-panel equation readout (smaller/secondary styling) so the in-canvas annotations remain the primary labels as in the source.
